# Order Management

This workspace describes the **Order Management** system and its interactions with external systems.

## Scope

- Customer-facing web store
- Order API and its components
- Fulfilment processing

- `workspace.dsl` — entry point, assembles the workspace with `!include`
- `people.dsl`, `software-systems.dsl`, `containers.dsl`, `components.dsl`, `relationships.dsl`, `views.dsl` — one concern per file

# Architecture Decisions

## ADR-001: Separate files per concern

We split the workspace into one file per concern (people, systems, containers, components, relationships, views) and assemble them with `!include` from `workspace.dsl`. This keeps diffs small and makes it easier to review changes.

## ADR-002: Documentation lives in `!docs`

Markdown pages are kept in the `!docs` folder so they are automatically picked up as documentation pages, keeping narrative content separate from the model.

# Order Management

This workspace models the **Order Management** system and its interactions with
external systems (Payment Gateway, Email Service). It is an example of the team's
multi-file Structurizr convention.

## Scope

- Customer-facing **Web Store**
- **Order API** and its components (Order Service, Order Repository, Payment Client)
- **Order Database** and **Fulfilment Worker**
- External **Payment Gateway** and **Email Service**

## File layout

The workspace is assembled from one file per concern, pulled together with `!include`:

| File | Concern |
| --- | --- |
| `workspace.dsl` | Entry point. Opens the `workspace`/`model` blocks and `!include`s the rest. |
| `people.dsl` | Actors (Customer, Support Agent). |
| `software-systems.dsl` | Software systems. `!include`s `containers.dsl` inside *Order Management*. |
| `containers.dsl` | Containers. `!include`s `components.dsl` inside *Order API*. |
| `components.dsl` | Components of the Order API. |
| `relationships.dsl` | All element-to-element relationships. |
| `views.dsl` | System context, container, component, and dynamic views. |
| `!docs/` | Markdown documentation pages, auto-included by Structurizr. |

Because this parser dialect nests containers inside their software system (and
components inside their container) rather than using `within`, the `!include`
directives are placed *inside* those blocks so each concern still lives in its own file.

## Views

- `SystemContext` — system context of Order Management
- `Containers` — container view of Order Management
- `OrderApiComponents` — component view of the Order API
- `PlaceOrder` — dynamic view of placing an order
